summary: Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, John Gombojab Hangin studied at Hokkaido University, Columbia University, and Indiana University. He held positions at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and was a full professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1989).

John Griffiths was an Indologist and historian/archaeologist who studied at the Royal College of Art from circa 1854 to 1859. He held a post at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art from circa 1865 to 1895.

Working in computational and other fields, John H. Holland studied under Arthur Burks from circa 1953 to 1959. He taught numerous students, including Edgar F. Codd, David E. Goldberg, and Stephanie Forrest.
John Hallett Batten worked in Indology and history/archaeology. He completed his education at Charterhouse School and the East India Company College, where he studied from circa 1827 to 1829.

Working in Indology and history/archaeology, John Henry Hutton was educated at Chigwell School and Worcester College, Oxford (circa 1904–1908). He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1909 to 1935.

John Henry Wright was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology who studied at Dartmouth and under Georg Curtius at Leipzig. He held professorships at Ohio State, Dartmouth, Johns Hopkins, the American School of Classical Studies at Athens, and Harvard (circa 1887–1908).

An Indologist, John Herbert Harington served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society. He was also an honorary professor of British government laws and regulations in India at Fort William College from circa 1801 to 1823.

John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies after studying at Scarborough College, the University of Edinburgh, and Oriel College, Oxford. His career included posts at Cornell, Princeton Theological Seminary, Cambridge, the University of Birmingham, and Claremont Graduate University (circa 1982–1992).

Crook studied Tibetology and Buddhist studies at Southampton and Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, and with Sheng Yen. He taught at the University of Bristol (circa 1963–1995) and held a fellowship at CASBS (circa 1968–1969).

John J. Holder, a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies, studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, advised by Geshe Lhundub Sopa and Lobsang Tendzin, and served as professor at Boston College (attested 1996–2007) and senior faculty advisor at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, John James Jones was educated at Aberystwyth University. He held the post of Deputy-Keeper in the Department of Printed Books at the National Library of Wales from circa 1943 to 1957.

John Jorgensen is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at the Australian National University, where he also held posts, alongside appointments at Griffith University and La Trobe University.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology, John Kieschnick held a position at the University of Bristol from circa 2005 to 2011. In 2011, he joined Stanford University as the Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies.

A philosopher educated at Lick-Wilmerding High School and the University of Oxford (circa 1963–1968), John Lane Bell held academic appointments at the London School of Economics (circa 1968–1989), the National University of Singapore, and the University of Western Ontario (circa 1989).

John Lockwood Kipling, who worked in history/archaeology and Indology, was educated at Woodhouse Grove School. He taught at the Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (circa 1865–1875) and served as Principal of the National College of Arts and Curator of Lahore Museum (1875–1893).

Working in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies, John M. Koller studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena, Charles A. Moore, and George T. Artola. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (attested 1988, 1999).

Rosenfield, who worked in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology, completed his PhD at Harvard under Benjamin Rowland. He held teaching posts at Iowa and UCLA before serving as professor (1965–1991), Harvard Art Museums Director, and Fogg Museum curator at Harvard.

John Marshall worked in history/archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studying at King's College, Cambridge, the British School at Athens, and under Arthur John Evans. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.
Working in Buddhist studies and religious studies, John Marston earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997. He subsequently held an academic post at El Colegio de México.
